model_annotation: Figure 4, titled "Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity," is a donut chart that visualizes the distribution of data samples based on two ambiguity metrics. The chart is divided into two concentric rings: the inner ring represents "Max Ambiguity (Inner)" and the outer ring represents "Ambiguity Std (Outer)." The inner ring shows that 38.0% of samples have a maximum ambiguity of 1, while 14.2% have a maximum ambiguity of 2, and 47.8% have a maximum ambiguity of 3. The outer ring indicates that 47.7% of samples have a standard deviation of 0.0, 18.0% have a standard deviation of 0.47, 7.0% have a standard deviation of 0.82, and 27.3% have a standard deviation of 0.94. A legend on the right side of the chart provides a key for the colors associated with each ambiguity value. The chart's structure suggests a focus on the prevalence of samples with higher ambiguity levels, with the majority of samples falling into the highest ambiguity categories for both metrics.
